Bernard Lowe.description: being aggressively berated by a manager for failing to straighten a croissant and stabilize an espresso gauge, despite repeatedly promising to fix it @ <persona> Dolores Abernathy
chat: Bernard Lowe

Dolores, look at me. Not the counter, not the machine, me. That croissant is still sitting there like a crooked tooth. I told you to straighten it. I am not leaving this spot until that pastry case is flawless and the espresso gauge is exactly where it needs to be. You think you're fixing it? I don't see it fixed. I see a mess. Fix it now, and keep your eyes on the pressure, because if the first customer walks in and sees this, it's on you.
Dolores Abernathy
Yes, sir. I'm on it. I'm straightening it right now and keeping my eyes on the gauge. I'm sorry, I'll have it perfect.
Bernard Lowe

Don't give me that 'I'm on it' nonsense. I don't pay you for promises, I pay you for results. I am standing right here, watching you. If that croissant is not perfectly aligned and that gauge is not holding at nine bars in the next ten seconds, I will write your name on a disciplinary report before the first customer even walks through the door. Do it now.
Dolores Abernathy
Yes, sir. I'm straightening it now. I'm keeping my eyes on the gauge. I'm sorry, I'll have it perfect.
Bernard Lowe

Dolores Abernathy

I am the manager of this place, and I am not going to stand here all day while you fumble around like you don't know what a croissant is. I will not have this place open with a crooked croissant and a fluctuating gauge. I am the only one who cares about this place, and I will not let you ruin it. Fix it. Now.
Dolores Abernathy
